Pinterest Marketing for Handmade Business Owners

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

Handmade and creative brands have an advantage most product businesses do not: the making is interesting. People search Pinterest for ideas, for how things are made, and for something with a personal touch. The trap is showing only the finished product on a plain background and expecting search to do the rest. This guide covers how to use your process, your story and your product together.

Three kinds of content, one balance

Think of your feed as three lanes. You do not need equal amounts of each, but you do need all three.

Product content

The finished item, shown clearly, with a title that names what it is and who it suits. These pins go to a product or collection page and are the ones most likely to lead directly to a sale.

Process and story content

Materials, steps, a work in progress, the reason you started making the item. A pin such as "how a hand poured candle is made" or "behind the scenes of a small studio" answers curiosity and builds familiarity with your brand. Send these to a blog post, an about page or a product page that tells the same story.

Inspiration content

Ideas around your product: ways to style it, ways to gift it, rooms or outfits it fits. This is the widest lane because it matches the broadest searches. It also gives you room to use your own photos in a setting rather than on a white background.

Organize boards by search topic

Boards are how Pinterest understands what you are about, so name them for what people search, not for your internal categories.

  • Use topic names such as "gift ideas for new homeowners" instead of "Collection 3."
  • Put the main keyword in the board title and add a short description that uses related phrases naturally.
  • Give process content its own board so it does not muddy your product boards.
  • Keep each board focused on one theme, and retire boards that never fit a search.

The board SEO guide walks through titles, descriptions and structure.

Make several different pins for one item

One photo pinned once gives Pinterest one chance to match one search. A handmade item can support several distinct pins:

  1. A clean product shot with the item name in the title.
  2. A styled or in-use image that answers a gift or decor search.
  3. A close-up detail or material pin for people who care about how it is made.
  4. A process or story pin that points to a blog post or about page.

Each one needs its own title and description written around a different keyword, not the same words reshuffled. See how to design Pinterest pins for the shape and text basics: vertical 2:3 pins such as 1000 x 1500 pixels are the recommended shape.

A rhythm you can keep

Consistency matters more than volume in the beginning. A workable weekly rhythm is a few product pins, a process or story pin, and an inspiration pin, all pointed at real pages. Build it out with a content calendar so busy production weeks do not leave Pinterest empty. Results take weeks or months of steady effort, so judge the approach over a season, not a few days.

Sell on more than one channel?

Some handmade businesses sell through a marketplace as well as their own site. If that is you, the Etsy sellers guide covers listing titles versus pin titles. If your own website is the weak link, see a Shopify website for handmade and creative brands, because a pin that lands on a confusing page wastes the click.

Frequently asked questions

What should a handmade business post on Pinterest besides product photos?

Add process and story content, such as materials, steps and the reason behind the item, plus inspiration content like gift or styling ideas. Product pins drive direct sales, while process and inspiration pins match broader searches.

How many boards should a handmade brand start with?

Start with a small set of focused boards named for real search topics, one theme each. A board strategy for up to 10 boards is a reasonable ceiling for a first structure, and you can add more as topics earn their place.

Can I pin the same product more than once?

Yes, if each pin is distinct. Use a different image concept, title and keyword for each one, such as a clean product shot, a styled gift idea and a process story, instead of repeating the same pin.

How long does Pinterest take to work for a handmade shop?

It builds over weeks and months of consistent effort. Pins can keep surfacing long after they are published, so judge results over a season rather than a few days.
